If the speed changes, the net acceleration is the perpendicular sum of the two and is tilted from the radius, so the statement is false; it holds only for uniform circular motion.

independent_solution: Constant speed means a_T = 0, so the acceleration is perpendicular to the velocity with magnitude v0^2/rho (rho = radius of curvature).
(a) false: the direction may change. (b) not necessarily: rho can be arbitrarily small (sharp turns), so |a| need not be bounded. (d) false: any curve at constant speed qualifies.
(c) true: for motion in a plane the velocity and all its changes lie in that plane, so the acceleration does too. Answer (c).
Released from the horizontal, the bob falls through h = L = 1.5 m, releasing m g L = m x 9.8 x 1.5 of potential energy.
95% becomes kinetic energy: (1/2) m v^2 = 0.95 m g L -> v = sqrt(2 x 0.95 x 9.8 x 1.5) = sqrt(27.93) = 5.28 m/s, about 5.3 m/s.
